voice.note: speaker → script/cast.json (voice, speed, pitch). Per line: speed (× the speaker's), pre/post (ms of silence before/after the voice), say (what is spoken, if not `text`), estVoice (s: the predicted voice length, tools/estimate.py; replaced by the real voice once tools/voice.py has run).

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI), Adi Parva, Adivamshavatarana sub-parva. CHECKED AGAINST CE 1.55.1–43 and 1.56.1–33. RESOLVED (the order of 1.55 in the CE): the father dead, the heroes come home from the forest and soon master Veda and bow (1.55.6); the Kurus cannot bear their fortune and fame (1.55.7); Duryodhana, Karna and Shakuni persecute them (1.55.8); poison for Bhima, who digests it (1.55.9); Bhima bound asleep and thrown into the Ganga (1.55.10–11); bitten by black snakes (1.55.12); Vidura watchful (1.55.13–14); the house of lac, the fire, the tunnel by Vidura's word (1.55.16–18); Hidimba killed (1.55.19); Ekachakra, Baka (1.55.20–21); Draupadi won; a year there; the return to Hastinapura (1.55.22); sent to Khandavaprastha (1.55.23–25), where they live many years and bring other kings under them (1.55.26–30); Arjuna in the forest a year and a month, then Dvaraka and Subhadra (1.55.31–34); the burning of Khandava, the bow Gandiva, Maya and the hall (1.55.35–38); Duryodhana's greed; Yudhishthira cheated at dice by Shakuni (1.55.39); the forest for twelve years and a thirteenth unknown (1.55.40); in the fourteenth they ask for their own and do not get it; then war (1.55.41); having destroyed everything and killed king Duryodhana, the Pandavas regain a kingdom most of whose people are gone (1.55.42, rajyam vidrutabhuyishtham: `war`, "a land laid waste"). Janamejaya: you have told it in brief; tell it again in full (1.56.1–3: `more`). RESOLVED (1.56): "in three years, rising daily, the sage Krishna Dvaipayana made this Mahabharata" is CE 1.56.32 (the plaque); "on law, profit, pleasure and release: what is here is elsewhere; what is not here is nowhere" is CE 1.56.33 (`here`; the four ends are on the plaque). The script's summary keeps the CE's order and leaves out Hidimba, Baka, Arjuna's exile and Khandava (pictures, or their own arcs); only two of its names are spoken. CE AGAINST VULGATE: the vulgate's summary is longer and Ganguli has Arjuna away eleven years and months; the CE has a year and a month (not voiced). No manuscript is shown.
structure: From episode 41 (the step-up; script/ARC-41-50.md): COLD OPEN (≤ 8 words, spoken by ≤ 2.8 s; the hook style rotates and never repeats the episode before) → title (hook post) → STORY from ≈ 4.5 s with the UNVOICED recap band → the episode stands alone (every name has an identifier in "names", shown as a plaque) → one question closed (loop.answeredBy), the previous one answered by 15 s (loop.prevAnsweredBy) → turn at 40–60 % after a real silence, a second silence where the story allows → one face close-up with a change of emotion → one signature shot → the cliffhanger with the source line → a ≤ 1.2 s NEXT › band that dissolves into frame 1. Per line: pal (the colour script: no hue for more than two lines), cam (≥ 4 distinct moves), tr (transitions born from the medium), amb / foley / music (three sound layers; ambLead / ambLag = J- and L-cuts). Gate: tools/gate.mjs.

loop.hookQuestion: Can the whole story fit in one breath?
loop.prevQuestion: How do you tell the whole Mahabharata in one breath?
loop.openQuestion: Why does the full story begin with a king, a fish and a ferry girl?

strings.episodeTitle: The Whole Story in One Breath
strings.recapLine: Asked how the great war began, Vyasa told his student to tell it all.
strings.nextTitle: The King, the Fish and the Ferry Girl

lines.text: The whole Mahabharata, in one breath.
lines.say: The whole Mahabharata, [p:100] in one breath.
lines.note: COLD OPEN (a number: one): a strip of small painted panels runs across the frame like a scroll being pulled: brothers, a burning house, dice, a forest, a field. The card under the strip.

lines.text: Vyasa's student began: all of it, in brief.
lines.say: Vyasa's student began: [p:200] all of it, [p:100] in brief.
lines.note: STORY 0 with the unvoiced recap band (top): the teal hall: Vaishampayana (plaque: Vaishampayana · Vyasa's student) before the seated king, Vyasa in gold beside him; he opens his hands.

lines.speaker: vaishampayana
lines.text: "Five brothers. A jealous cousin, Duryodhana, who wanted them dead."
lines.say: Five brothers. [p:300] A jealous cousin, [p:100] Duryodhana, [p:100] who wanted them dead.
lines.note: PANEL 1 (seat-ivory: a court): five young men in a row, one behind another, entering a pillared court; across from them one prince, turned away, his hand a fist (plaque: Duryodhana · the jealous cousin). Each panel has its own colour and its own move; brush wipes between.

lines.speaker: vaishampayana
lines.text: "Poison. A house built to burn. They lived."
lines.say: Poison. [p:300] A house built to burn. [p:300] They lived.
lines.note: PANEL 2 (hearth-amber): a cup; a great house of red lacquer going up in flames; under the ground line, in section, six small figures walking a tunnel, lit by one lamp. A tilt from the roof to the tunnel.

lines.speaker: vaishampayana
lines.text: "A princess won, Draupadi. A kingdom built."
lines.say: A princess won, [p:100] Draupadi. [p:300] A kingdom built.
lines.note: PANEL 3 (crystal-sky): a bow drawn at a target high on a pole; a woman with a garland (plaque: Draupadi · princess of Panchala); a crane up to a white city on a river.

lines.speaker: vaishampayana
lines.text: "Then a crooked game of dice took it all."
lines.say: Then a crooked game of dice [p:100] took it all.
lines.note: PANEL 4 · THE TURN (≈ 45 %) after a real silence · THE SIGNATURE SHOT (dice-vermilion): from directly above, a dicing cloth: the dice fall, turn and stop; on each side hands; the city, the crowns, the brothers' ornaments slide across the cloth to one side. A push in on the dice.

lines.speaker: vaishampayana
lines.text: "Twelve years in the forest. One more in hiding."
lines.say: Twelve years in the forest. [p:250] One more [p:60] in hiding.
lines.note: PANEL 5 (exile-forest): six figures walking away under great trees, seen from behind; twelve small moons cross the canopy in an arc; a thirteenth is hidden by a leaf.

lines.speaker: vaishampayana
lines.text: "They asked for their kingdom, and were refused. So came the war. They won back a land laid waste."
lines.say: They asked for their kingdom, [p:120] and were refused. [p:300] So came the war. [p:350] They won back [p:60] a land laid waste.
lines.note: PANEL 6 (war-iron; answers the hook): an open hand held out, a closed door; then a tilt down from banners to two armies facing each other, small, innumerable, no blood; on "laid waste" the field is empty and grey: five small figures and one woman standing, a crown on the ground, empty houses behind; no triumph. The strip of panels closes.

lines.speaker: janamejaya
lines.text: "That was brief. Now tell me all of it."
lines.say: That was brief. [p:300] Now tell me [p:60] all of it.
lines.note: STORY 8 (a second real silence before it) · THE CLOSE-UP: the king's face: struck, then hungry for more (the brows lift, he leans in, a breath) (plaque: Janamejaya · the king who asked).

lines.speaker: vaishampayana
lines.text: "What is here is found elsewhere. What is not here is nowhere."
lines.say: What is here [p:60] is found elsewhere. [p:250] What is not here [p:80] is nowhere.
lines.note: STORY 9: Vaishampayana, an open hand lifted, reciting (no manuscript: the text has a recital); a slow orbit; behind him Vyasa, eyes closed, gold (plaques: Vyasa · composed it in three years; under the line, small: on law, wealth, love and freedom).

lines.text: So he began again: with a king, a fish, and a ferry girl.
lines.say: So he began again: [p:150] with a king, [p:80] a fish, [p:80] and a ferry girl.
lines.note: NEXT 1 (the catalog's cliffhanger): a lamp-glow match cut to deep river blue: three images on the three beats: a crown in the sky, a silver fish turning, a girl's hand on an oar. The source line (top).
